claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is initially in a high-temperature BCC phase.
Diffusion-mediated atomic ordering during cooling and thermal aging drives phase evolution in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7.
Diffusion-mediated ordering forms short-range ordered clusters in the BCC matrix.
The short-range ordered clusters act as nucleation sites for ordered secondary phases.
Slow cooling provides sufficient atomic mobility for diffusion-controlled ordering.
Moderate-temperature thermal aging provides sufficient atomic mobility for diffusion-controlled ordering.
Differential atomic mobilities produce local chemical ordering during slow cooling and aging.
Local chemical ordering reduces the nucleation barrier for ordered secondary phases.
Reduced nucleation barriers promote growth of ordered secondary phases at the expense of the BCC matrix.
Rapid quenching retains a predominantly BCC structure with minimal atomic ordering.
Relative to rapidly quenched samples, slow-cooled and aged samples will exhibit additional XRD peaks or peak splitting.
Slow-cooled and aged samples will contain nanoscale ordered clusters observable by TEM.
Nanoscale ordered clusters will develop into larger ordered domains during aging.
Ordering reactions may produce exothermic transitions detectable by DSC.
The proposed mechanism should not apply when stress-driven or other transformation mechanisms dominate.

contradictions.description: The baseline is described as rapidly quenched and therefore retaining minimal ordering, but the falsification design subsequently ages all samples at a diffusion-active temperature. Because the mechanism itself states that thermal aging promotes ordering, the nominal quenched baseline may also order and is not equivalent to an unaged quenched state. The intervention field also implies aging only after slow cooling, whereas the experiment design applies aging to both cooling groups.
